_comment: The copy rules, as data rather than as prose, so a lint step can enforce them instead of a person remembering them. Pipedia BRAND-KIT §13 is the written version and must agree with this file.
_english_note: British English — spelling, vocabulary and idiom. Set 2026-08-25, reversing the American-English rule adopted 2026-08-24. Watch the idioms rather than the spellings: the spellings are easy and the idioms are what slip through.
_convert_note: 'line' -> 'queue' and 'more expensive' -> 'dearer' are context-dependent and must never be applied mechanically; a line of CSS is not a queue. They are listed so a human reviewing copy considers them, not so a script rewrites them.

punctuation._note: Never an em dash in copy the audience sees or hears: captions, on-screen text, titles, teases, descriptions, voice-over. Set 2026-09-03, after one reached a rendered Pipedia episode. Use the punctuation the sentence needs instead of one mark doing four jobs, and a seven-year-old reading along has met all four of these and not the dash.
punctuation._not_retroactive: Pipedia's Money and Business ship about fifty em dashes on screen between them and are published. Nothing is re-cut. A style rule adopted mid-project needs an explicit statement of what it leaves alone; this is it.

_exempt_note: YouTube tags and hashtags are search strings, not prose: they are spelled the way people actually type them, which is why 'business math for kids' stays. A hashtag is the same object as a YouTube tag wearing a '#', so it is exempt for the same reason and not a second rule — '#MathForKids' can sit under a caption that says 'maths'. Code, paths and identifiers are spelled the way the language spells them. Quoted material keeps its source's spelling. Editorial notes are a consumer's own working documents — a script's director notes, a comment in a build file — and are not copy: they are exempt from the punctuation rule for the same reason code is exempt from the spelling one. The DIALOGUE inside such a document is not exempt, because it is the source of a caption and a voice-over.

currency._note: Bare $, no country prefix. BRAND-KIT §13, and NOT affected by the English variant — the audience is self-filtering and localisation is a separate build.
